name: Release

# Publishing a GitHub release builds the .deb, attaches it to the release and
# adds it to the signed apt repository on the gh-pages branch.
#
# Two jobs so that no code from the build ever shares a runner with the
# signing key:
#   build - compiles dependencies and runs cargo; no secrets; write token only
#           to attach the .deb to the release; no cache
#   apt   - holds the signing key; runs no cargo, only gpg and apt-ftparchive

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  # To redo a release's packaging by hand, from the Actions tab.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: Release tag to package, such as v0.1.0
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

# One release at a time: both jobs write to shared places.
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag }}

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # to attach the .deb to the release
    steps:
      # Third-party actions are pinned by commit, not by movable tag.
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.TAG }} # the release's own source, also when run by hand
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Check the tag matches the version
        run: |
          version=$(cargo metadata --locked --no-deps --format-version 1 \
            | jq -r '.packages[] | select(.name == "cosmic-ext-nightlight") | .version')
          if [ "$TAG" != "v$version" ]; then
            echo "Tag $TAG does not match the package version $version." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            build-essential pkg-config cmake \
            libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libegl1-mesa-dev libgbm-dev \
            libdrm-dev libinput-dev libudev-dev libseat-dev libssl-dev \
            libfontconfig-dev libfreetype-dev libexpat1-dev

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable
        with:
          toolchain: stable

      # No rust-cache here on purpose: a release is built clean.
      # Exact versions, bumped by hand in a reviewed change (Dependabot does
      # not track crates installed this way).
      - name: Install just and cargo-deb
        run: cargo install --locked just@1.59.0 cargo-deb@3.8.0

      - name: Build the .deb
        run: just deb

      - name: Attach it to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          cd target/debian
          for deb in cosmic-ext-nightlight_*.deb; do
            sha256sum "$deb" > "$deb.sha256"
            gh release upload "$TAG" "$deb" "$deb.sha256" --clobber -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          done

  apt:
    # Signs only: downloads the finished .deb and runs gpg and apt-ftparchive.
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # to push the gh-pages branch
    steps:
      # The publishing script from the default branch, which may be newer
      # than the release being packaged.
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          persist-credentials: false

      # This one keeps its credentials: the last step pushes with them.
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          ref: gh-pages
          path: site

      - name: Install apt-ftparchive
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends apt-utils

      - name: Download the .deb from the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          mkdir debs
          gh release download "$TAG" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -D debs \
            -p 'cosmic-ext-nightlight_*.deb' -p 'cosmic-ext-nightlight_*.deb.sha256'
          cd debs && sha256sum -c ./*.sha256

      - name: Add it to the repository and sign
        env:
          APT_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.APT_SIGNING_KEY }}
          KEY_ID: ${{ vars.APT_SIGNING_KEY_ID }}
        run: |
          GNUPGHOME=$(mktemp -d)
          export GNUPGHOME
          trap 'rm -rf "$GNUPGHOME"' EXIT
          printf '%s\n' "$APT_SIGNING_KEY" | gpg --batch --quiet --import
          scripts/publish-apt.sh site "$KEY_ID" debs/cosmic-ext-nightlight_*.deb

      - name: Publish the repository
        run: |
          cd site
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Repository unchanged."
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "apt repository: cosmic-ext-nightlight ${TAG#v}"
          git push

#!/bin/sh
# Rebuild the signed apt repository that GitHub Pages serves.
#
# Usage: scripts/publish-apt.sh <site-dir> <key-id> [new .deb files...]
#
# <site-dir> is a checkout of the gh-pages branch. New .deb files are added
# to its pool (earlier ones stay, so apt can still find them); the package
# index and the signed Release files are then generated again from the whole
# pool. Signing uses the key <key-id> from the keyring in $GNUPGHOME.
# Needs apt-ftparchive (apt-utils) and gpg.
set -eu

if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 <site-dir> <key-id> [new .deb files...]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
site=$1
key=$2
shift 2

pool=pool/main/c/cosmic-ext-nightlight
dist=dists/stable
mkdir -p "$site/$pool" "$site/$dist/main/binary-amd64"
for deb in "$@"; do
    cp "$deb" "$site/$pool/"
done

cd "$site"
apt-ftparchive packages pool > "$dist/main/binary-amd64/Packages"
gzip -9 -n -k -f "$dist/main/binary-amd64/Packages"

# Written beside the dists tree first: apt-ftparchive would otherwise list
# the half-written Release file in itself.
apt-ftparchive \
    -o APT::FTPArchive::Release::Origin=deepthinker2001 \
    -o APT::FTPArchive::Release::Label="Night Light for COSMIC" \
    -o APT::FTPArchive::Release::Suite=stable \
    -o APT::FTPArchive::Release::Codename=stable \
    -o APT::FTPArchive::Release::Architectures=amd64 \
    -o APT::FTPArchive::Release::Components=main \
    -o APT::FTPArchive::Release::Description="Night Light for COSMIC: a panel applet that toggles a night light" \
    release "$dist" > Release.new
mv Release.new "$dist/Release"

gpg --batch --yes --local-user "$key" --clearsign -o "$dist/InRelease" "$dist/Release"
gpg --batch --yes --local-user "$key" --armor --detach-sign -o "$dist/Release.gpg" "$dist/Release"
gpg --batch --yes --armor --export "$key" > key.gpg

# Serve the files as they are, without GitHub Pages' Jekyll processing.
touch .nojekyll
echo "Repository in $site rebuilt and signed with $key."

### With apt (recommended)

Add the signed repository once; updates then arrive with your normal system
updates:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://deepthinker2001.github.io/cosmic-ext-nightlight/key.gpg \\
  | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/cosmic-ext-nightlight.gpg

```

Then [add it to the panel](#add-it-to-the-panel).

To update to a new version: `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`, or just
install your system updates as usual.

Remove it with `sudo apt remove cosmic-ext-nightlight`. To also stop trusting
the repository, delete `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cosmic-ext-nightlight.list`
and `/usr/share/keyrings/cosmic-ext-nightlight.gpg`.

### From a release

Download the `.deb` (and its `.sha256`, to check the download) from the
[releases page](../../releases/latest), then:

```sh
sha256sum -c cosmic-ext-nightlight_*.deb.sha256
sudo apt install ./cosmic-ext-nightlight_*.deb
```

This does not update itself; use the apt repository above for that.

To build from source instead, see
[Build and install from source](#build-and-install-from-source) below.

'''

EOF

python3 -I - <<'EOF'
p='docs/RELEASING.md'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('## How a release is built')
new='''## How a release is built

Publishing a GitHub release runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`. It has two
jobs, so that code from the build never shares a runner with the signing key:

- `build` checks out the release's tag, checks the tag equals `v` plus the
  `version` in `Cargo.toml`, builds the `.deb` with `just deb` (no cache; `just`
  and `cargo-deb` at fixed versions) and attaches it and its `.sha256` to the
  release. It has no secrets.
- `apt` holds the signing key. It downloads that `.deb`, checks its checksum,
  adds it to the apt repository on the `gh-pages` branch with
  `scripts/publish-apt.sh`, signs the repository and pushes the branch.
  GitHub Pages serves the branch at
  `https://deepthinker2001.github.io/cosmic-ext-nightlight`.

The workflow can also be run by hand from the Actions tab with a tag, to
redo the packaging of an existing release.

The `gh-pages` branch holds only generated files: `pool/` (every published
`.deb`), `dists/stable/` (`Packages`, `Release`, `InRelease`, `Release.gpg`),
`key.gpg` (the public key) and `.nojekyll`. Never edit it by hand.

## One-time setup

### The signing key

On a trusted machine:

```sh
gpg --quick-generate-key "cosmic-ext-nightlight apt repository <you@example.com>" ed25519 sign 5y
gpg --list-keys --with-colons you@example.com   # the "fpr" line is the full fingerprint
```

The key must have no passphrase, because the workflow signs unattended (use
a key made only for this repository). gpg saves a revocation certificate at
`~/.gnupg/openpgp-revocs.d/<FINGERPRINT>.rev`; copy it and a backup of the
private key somewhere offline. Note the expiry date: extend the key before
then (`gpg --quick-set-expire FINGERPRINT 5y`, then update the secret and
rerun the workflow for the latest tag), or apt will refuse the repository.

### Secret and variable

In the repository settings (or with `gh`):

```sh
gpg --armor --export-secret-keys FINGERPRINT | gh secret set APT_SIGNING_KEY
gh variable set APT_SIGNING_KEY_ID --body FINGERPRINT
```

- Secret `APT_SIGNING_KEY`: the ASCII-armoured private key. Never print it.
- Variable `APT_SIGNING_KEY_ID`: the key's fingerprint (not secret).

Also add a tag ruleset protecting `v*` (restrict who can create, update and
delete those tags). Only the `apt` job reads the secret.

### The gh-pages branch and GitHub Pages

Create an empty branch with a first commit, once:

```sh
git switch --orphan gh-pages
git commit --allow-empty -m "Start the apt repository"
git push origin gh-pages
git switch main
```

Then in Settings → Pages, set the source to **Deploy from a branch**, branch
`gh-pages`, folder `/ (root)`. The first release fills the branch in.

## Cut a release

1. Make sure CI is green on `main`.
2. Set `version` in `Cargo.toml` (for example `0.2.0`) and commit the
   updated `Cargo.lock` (CI builds with `--locked`). A version is never
   reused: apt caches packages by version, so a fix is a new version.
3. Publish a GitHub release whose tag is `v` plus that version:
   `gh release create v0.2.0 --target main --title "0.2.0" --generate-notes`
   (or Releases → Draft a new release on GitHub). Don't attach a `.deb`
   yourself.
4. Watch Actions → Release: `build` and `apt` should both pass. Check the
   release lists the `.deb` and `.sha256`, and on a machine with the
   repository added, `sudo apt update && apt policy cosmic-ext-nightlight`
   shows the new version as the candidate.

If the workflow fails, fix the cause on `main` and rerun it for the tag:
`gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v0.2.0`. The build uses the source at the
tag; the publishing script comes from `main`. If the fix has to be in the
source, make a new version instead.

## Not tested

None of this has run on GitHub: the workflow, `scripts/publish-apt.sh` with
real GitHub Pages, and the signed repository with a real apt client. The first
release is the first test, so after it, install from the repository on a clean
machine. `build` and `apt` use `ubuntu-latest`; the `.deb`'s libc6 minimum
comes from that runner.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s[:a]+new)
EOF

Release via signed APT repo on gh-pages

Replace the tag-triggered GPG-signed release with the dimmer pattern: on
release published (or manual dispatch), build attaches .deb + .sha256, apt

text:
The release now follows the dimmer pattern: publishing a GitHub release builds the `.deb` and adds it to a signed APT repo on `gh-pages`. Nothing has run on GitHub. I did run `scripts/publish-apt.sh` locally with a throwaway key and a dummy `.deb`. It produced the expected pool, `Packages`, `Release`, `InRelease`, `Release.gpg`, `key.gpg` and `.nojekyll`, and `gpg --verify` accepted `InRelease`. I also checked that the workflow YAML parses and the script passes `sh -n`.

- **Workflow:** `.github/workflows/release.yml` triggers on release published and on manual dispatch with a tag.

## How a release is built

Publishing a GitHub release runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`. It has three
jobs, so that code from the build never shares a runner with the signing key
or a write token:

- `build` checks out the release's tag, checks the tag equals `v` plus the
  `version` in `Cargo.toml`, builds the `.deb` with `just deb` (no cache; `just`
  and `cargo-deb` at fixed versions) and attaches it and its `.sha256` to the
  release. It has no secrets.
- `apt` holds the signing key. It downloads that `.deb`, checks its checksum,
  adds it to the apt repository on the `gh-pages` branch with
  `scripts/publish-apt.sh`, signs the repository and pushes the branch.
  GitHub Pages serves the branch at
  `https://deepthinker2001.github.io/cosmic-ext-nightlight`.

The workflow can also be run by hand from the Actions tab with a tag, to
redo the packaging of an existing release.

The `gh-pages` branch holds only generated files: `pool/` (every published
`.deb`), `dists/stable/` (`Packages`, `Release`, `InRelease`, `Release.gpg`),
`key.gpg` (the public key) and `.nojekyll`. Never edit it by hand.
